transcript.text: I want to flag something I personally observed during last year's large-group gratitude round. On three separate occasions, remote or quieter employees were called on unexpectedly and became visibly uncomfortable. I didn't include this in the event retrospective since it focused on attendance and logistics, but I think it's an important constraint to consider as we plan this year's format and participation rules.

transcript.text: I need to flag an HR constraint for this year's event. I want to make sure this is factored into the participation rules and communications plan before Elena signs off.

transcript.text: Thank you all for sharing these constraints. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my decision. Marcus, you've flagged that last year's spontaneous call-outs made remote and quieter employees uncomfortable — so we need to move away from that format. Sofia, you need the event scheduled within the 15:00–16:00 window on the proposed day due to your caregiving arrangement. Priyanka, HR requires the event to be opt-in with an asynchronous recognition route for non-attendees. And Jonah, Internal Communications has already promised remote staff representatives a written appreciation board with private nominations rather than spontaneous speaking. These all point in the same direction — a written, opt-in format with no spontaneous call-outs, scheduled in Sofia's window, and an asynchronous option for those who can't attend. Let me formalize this into a decision.
